caption:
12,462 flights were canceled on Friday, Nov. 13, the FAA says, after a telecom failure stopped departures at every U.S. airport for hours.

Here's the rule most travelers never hear: if the airline cancels your flight and you turn down the rebooking, it owes you a cash refund — the full fare plus taxes and fees — not a voucher. Paid by credit card? It's due within 7 business days. That's a U.S. Department of Transportation rule, in force since 2024.

My take: airlines push vouchers because a voucher keeps your money. Thanksgiving travel starts next week — know the rule before you need it.
